drug_class: Intravenous Nutritional Supplement / Parenteral Nutrition Component
purpose: This medicine is a special liquid nutrition given directly into your vein when you cannot eat enough food by mouth or through a feeding tube. It provides your body with protein building blocks called amino acids, which your body needs to heal, maintain muscle, and stay strong. Doctors use it for patients recovering from surgery, serious illness, or other conditions where normal eating is not possible.
how_it_works: Think of amino acids as the individual bricks your body uses to build and repair proteins. When this solution is dripped into your vein through an IV, your body absorbs these building blocks directly into your bloodstream. Your cells then use them to make proteins that repair tissues, support your immune system, and keep your organs working properly — just like the protein you would normally get from food like meat, eggs, or beans.
common_side_effects: Some people may experience nausea, mild fever, or flushing. You might notice swelling, redness, or discomfort at the IV site. Some patients have changes in their blood sugar levels. Occasionally, people feel tired or have headaches.
warnings: This solution should only be given by trained medical staff in a clinical setting. It is not safe if you have severe kidney or liver disease unless your doctor specifically approves it. Your blood sugar, kidney function, and electrolytes (body salts) will need to be checked regularly while you receive this. Never try to use or adjust this IV solution on your own. If you notice swelling, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or high fever, tell your nurse or doctor right away.
typical_dosing: Your doctor and pharmacist will calculate exactly how much you need based on your weight, health condition, and nutritional needs. It is usually given as a slow, continuous drip through an IV line over many hours each day. The dose is very individualized, so it will be different for every patient and adjusted regularly based on your lab results and how you are doing.
